exposure: Sociodemographic factors (parents' marital/registration status, mother's country of birth, maternal age, area deprivation)
cohort: The study included 4.6 million live singleton births in England and Wales between 2006 and 2012, covering various ethnic groups.
finding: Substantial ethnic disparity in risk of unexplained infant death exists in England and Wales, with Black Caribbean babies having the highest risk and Indian babies the lowest, which is not primarily attributable to preterm birth or area deprivation.
followup_time: During infancy (up to 1 year after birth)
gest_age: Included as an adjustment factor (gestational age at birth)
